clue.text: Vessel's radar finally thrown out by big wave

definitions.note: read as 'Vessel is', the 's being a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: a letter thrown out by a word is removed from inside it

parts.note: a breaker is a large wave crashing on the shore

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word radar

explanation.surface: A ship's radar is knocked out by a huge wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R, the last letter of 'radar'; 'thrown out by' removes that R from BREAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup or lab glass, a kind of vessel for holding liquid.

clue.text: They know about eating pie cooked with preserves

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of pie being worked over into a new form

parts.note: to cure meat or fish is to preserve it, so preserves gives cures

explanation.surface: Gourmets are familiar with a pie made with jam and pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges PIE into EPI; 'preserves' is a verb here, giving CURES, not jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicures are connoisseurs of fine food, people with expert knowledge of eating well.

clue.text: Derby area known to Scots, not originally favoured

parts.note: in Scots, kent is the past participle of ken, to know

indicators.note: not originally means the opening letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: favoured by fortune means lucky

explanation.surface: A Derby region familiar to Scotsmen, though not favoured at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kentucky Derby is the famous US horse race, so 'Derby area' misleads towards the English county town. 'not originally' removes L from LUCKY to leave UCKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state hosts the Kentucky Derby, the horse race at Churchill Downs in Louisville.

clue.text: Meet again about acting — priest in church

parts.note: re is a short form for about, concerning

indicators.note: in places acting and priest within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
on stage, an actor is on, that is acting
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon, a senior priest

explanation.surface: A gathering again about someone playing a priest in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, short for Venerable, is the formal title of an archdeacon; CE is the Church of England. The dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, so it means to meet again.

clue.text: Tender put in for management of Cheviots?

definitions.text: Tender put in for management of Cheviots?

parts.words: Tender put in for management of Cheviots?
parts.note: a tender is a bid, but read as one who tends: the person placed in charge of Cheviot sheep

explanation.surface: A bid has been submitted to manage the Cheviot hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheviots are a breed of sheep from the hills on the English-Scottish border; 'tender' means one who tends, not a business bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks after a flock tends sheep, so the herder is a tender of Cheviots.

clue.text: It's involved with sand and shells here up north

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters being tangled and twisted together

parts.note: the fodder needs shell, singular

explanation.surface: Sandy beaches and seashells are found in this northern spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ITS SAND AND SHELL; as printed, 'shells' gives one S too many, apparently a lost apostrophe (shell's).
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands lie far north of mainland Scotland, the northernmost part of Britain.

clue.text: Greek hero takes agent to court when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: takes to court means sues, and the agent is a rep, a representative

explanation.surface: A Greek hero sues his agent after being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns SUES REP upside down in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseus is the hero of Greek myth who beheaded the Gorgon Medusa.

clue.text: For example, Asian actor's initial obsession with self

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example
an Omani comes from Oman, in Asia

indicators.note: initial picks out the opening letter of the word actor's

explanation.surface: An Asian actor whose early fixation was himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes A from 'actor's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an excessive preoccupation with oneself.

clue.text: Tory's den, clumsily built without mortar

indicators.note: clumsily built suggests the letters being put together in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A Conservative's study was thrown up carelessly with no cement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily built' rearranges TORYSDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drystone walls are built of stones fitted together with no mortar holding them.

clue.text: Crown left in small boat

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the small boat

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried on a ship

explanation.surface: A crown has been left inside a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnacle and crown both mean the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: In vogue, like flutes

definitions.meaning: having grooves, as a fluted column or glass has

explanation.surface: Fashionable, just like flutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Groovy is sixties slang for fashionable, and literally means full of grooves, as fluting is.

clue.text: Description of the fall of unions in manual trades

indicators.note: in places the unions inside the rearranged letters
trades means swaps, so the letters of manual are exchanged around

parts.note: TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: An account of how unions collapsed in the manual trades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trades' rearranges the word manual to AUMNAL. 'the fall' is the US word for autumn, not a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumnal is the adjective for autumn, the season Americans call the fall.

clue.text: Withdraw part of army? That's impossible

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
can't, as in it can't be done

explanation.surface: Pull back a section of the army? That can't be done.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to take back a statement or belief formally, to withdraw it.

clue.text: Enthusiasm shown in a thousand directions!

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, from kilo
compass points E, E, N, N, E, S, S

explanation.surface: Eagerness displayed in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness is eagerness, an enthusiastic wish to do something.

clue.text: Outrageous that sloppy group captures old missile maker

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a shower is British slang for an incompetent bunch of people
OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: It's outrageous how a slack gang seized an old arms manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: A shot tower dropped molten lead from a height to form round shot for guns; 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot tower was a tall building where lead shot, small missiles for guns, was made.

clue.text: Always quiet inside, showing evidence of recent fire

indicators.note: inside puts the letters for quiet within the word for always

parts.note: ay is a poetic word for always
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Ever silent within, showing signs of a recent blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means covered with ash, the residue left behind by a fire.

clue.text: Half-inch painting by Kandinsky, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a non-figurative work like those of Kandinsky

explanation.surface: Half an inch of a picture by Kandinsky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal; to abstract is to remove or steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to take away or purloin, and Kandinsky pioneered abstract art.

clue.text: Russian gallery rejecting Frenchman's legacy

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so a letter is taken out of the gallery

parts.note: the Hermitage is the great art museum in St Petersburg
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Russian museum turns down a Frenchman's bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from past generations, a legacy.

clue.text: Head removed from second fish

indicators.note: head removed means the opening letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a shake is a moment, as in in two shakes

explanation.surface: Decapitating a fish in a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake is a sea fish of the cod family, common on British menus.

clue.text: Display sound weaving machine, one long in the family

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word for display is pronounced

parts.note: to air views is to display them
a loom is a machine for weaving cloth

explanation.surface: Show off a sturdy weaving machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is the homophone signal here, not an adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession passed down a family through generations.

clue.text: Plant of reasonable size in outskirts of Kirovograd

indicators.note: in places the middle phrase within the outer letters
outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Kirovograd

parts.note: not wee, wee being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A plant of decent size grows on the edge of a Ukrainian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives K and D, the first and last letters of Kirovograd.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotweed is a plant, notably the invasive Japanese knotweed.

clue.text: Kentish child taken outside just after interval

parts.note: Kent is in SE (south-east) England

indicators.note: taken outside means the word for child goes around the other piece

parts.note: a mite is a small child
on means immediately after, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: A child from Kent is taken out just after the break.
explanation.walkthrough: The result of the insertion is MITONE. Kent is a county in south-east England, hence 'Kentish' for SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the musical interval of half a tone, as between adjacent piano keys.

clue.text: Circle infiltrated by FBI agents — or part of one

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the second piece gets inside the first

parts.note: a set is a circle of people
G-men, government men, are FBI agents

explanation.surface: A social circle penetrated by FBI agents, or some of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section of a circle cut off by a chord.

clue.text: Slender guy, not posh -—- I forget his name

parts.note: slender means thin

indicators.note: not posh means dropping the letter used for upper-class

parts.note: taken as written, before the deletion

explanation.surface: A skinny, unrefined man whose name I can't recall.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class or posh; 'not posh' drops it from GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingy is a placeholder word used when a name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Scholars retail it in translation

indicators.note: in translation suggests the letters being turned into another form

explanation.surface: Academics sell it on in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges RETAILIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, literary class, scholars and intellectuals.

clue.text: Alphabetical guide introducing a meadow plant?

indicators.note: introducing means coming in front of what follows

parts.note: an A-Z is an alphabetical guide or street map
a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: An alphabetical guide introduces a plant of the meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the standard London street atlas, organised alphabetically.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub related to the rhododendron.

clue.text: Recent arrival runs after member of Thackeray's family

indicators.note: after puts runs behind the family member

parts.note: Thackeray's novel The Newcomes follows the Newcome family
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A newcomer chases after a Thackeray relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone who has only just arrived.

clue.text: Entered into obligations for ten years

indicators.note: into places the word for entered inside the obligations

parts.note: ties are bonds or obligations
went in, so went

explanation.surface: Signed up to commitments for a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are a decade, ten years such as 1920 to 1929.

clue.text: Willing me to come in for a treatment

indicators.note: to come in for means to take the place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: ready means willing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being keen for me to stand in as a substitute for some therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come in for' means replace: ME takes the place of the A in READY. It is not an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or medicine, a treatment for illness.
